steps.name: prompt
steps.text: Write the introduction for our paper ED-NeRF, a method for editing 3D NeRF scenes from text prompts efficiently by working in a latent space. Review NeRF and text-to-3D progress, explain why existing NeRF editing methods are slow or unstable, and introduce our approach.

steps.name: skeleton_outline
steps.text:
- Progress in neural implicit 3D representations and text-to-3D generation
- Editing pre-trained NeRFs: open problem; CLIP-based methods
- Diffusion-based editing methods and their drawbacks
- Our approach: ED-NeRF

steps.name: detailed_outline
steps.text:
- Background
  - neural implicit representation for embedding 3D images in networks: remarkable progress
  - render from all angles from limited training viewpoints
  - NeRF: radiance fields with simple MLP; improvements via advanced architectures / modified encoding
  - alternative: directly optimize voxel points as rendering sources, not implicit networks; very short training time
  - beyond 2D data in 3D: generating novel 3D objects
  - CLIP -> implicit networks generating objects from text prompts
  - text-to-image diffusion (Stable Diffusion), score distillation sampling (SDS) conveys text-to-image representation to NeRF
- Editing pre-trained NeRF
  - open problem: keep original 3D integrity while making desired modifications
  - early: text-conditioned editing with pre-trained CLIP fine-tuning NeRF params
  - weaknesses: CLIP performance limits; high-resolution rendering during training -> much time
- Diffusion-based editing
  - leverage expressiveness of models like Stable Diffusion
  - direct SDS + additional regularizations: time-consuming, unstable; full-resolution rendering + SDS loss limits
  - manipulate NeRF training images with text-guided image translation: periodic translation during training -> long training time
- ED-NeRF
  - goal: efficient, effective 3D scene editing from text prompts only
  - NeRF operates in latent space, like Latent-NeRF -> lower time/compute
  - naive latent rendering of real scenes -> drop in view synthesis, no geometric consistency in latent space
  - analysis of latent generation process -> novel refinement layer
  - extend Delta Denoising Score (DDS) (2D editing via SDS) to 3D -> high-performance editing, affordable cost even with Stable Diffusion
  - name: ED-NeRF (EDiting NeRF)

steps.name: partial_draft
steps.text:
In recent years there has been remarkable progress in neural implicit representation for embedding three-dimensional images in neural networks. Because of this, it is now possible to render images from all angles with only a limited set of training viewpoints. Starting from the first well-known work, the Neural Radiance Field (NeRF), which trained radiance fields with a simple MLP network, various improved techniques have been proposed that are based on advanced network architectures or modified encoding. As an alternative, several methods proposed to directly optimize voxel points that serve as sources for rendering, skipping the traditional approach of putting all the information inside implicit networks. These methods became prominent because they can train radiance fields in a remarkably short time. Besides representing existing 2D image data in 3D space, recent research has also explored ways of generating completely new 3D objects. With text-to-image embedding models like CLIP, various methods have been proposed to train implicit networks that generate new objects only from text prompts. This trend got faster with text-to-image diffusion generation models such as Stable Diffusion, especially through score distillation sampling (SDS), which conveys the representation of the text-to-image model to the NeRF model.

However, editing pre-trained 3D implicit networks according to specific conditions is still an open problem because of the constraints of the task: the integrity of the original 3D images has to be maintained while making the desired modifications. As initial work, several approaches tried to edit pre-trained NeRF models based on text conditions, using the pre-trained CLIP model to fine-tune the NeRF model parameters. But these methods have notable weaknesses, like the performance limitations of the CLIP model itself and the need to render high-resolution images during training, which takes a lot of time.

- Diffusion-based editing
  - use expressiveness of Stable Diffusion-type models
  - direct SDS + regularizations: slow, unstable (full-resolution rendering, SDS loss limits)
  - text-guided image translation of NeRF training images: periodic translation -> long training time
- ED-NeRF
  - edit 3D scenes efficiently and effectively from text prompts only
  - operate in NeRF latent space like Latent-NeRF -> lower time and compute
  - naive latent rendering of real scenes -> view synthesis drop (no geometric consistency) -> analysis + novel refinement layer
  - extend Delta Denoising Score (DDS) to 3D -> high-performance editing at affordable cost even with Stable Diffusion
  - named ED-NeRF (EDiting NeRF)

steps.name: rough_draft
steps.text:
In recent years there has been remarkable progress in neural implicit representation for embedding three-dimensional images in neural networks. Because of this, it is now possible to render images from all angles with only a limited set of training viewpoints. Starting from the first well-known work, the Neural Radiance Field (NeRF), which trained radiance fields with a simple MLP network, various improved techniques have been proposed that are based on advanced network architectures or modified encoding. As an alternative, several methods proposed to directly optimize voxel points that serve as sources for rendering, skipping the traditional approach of putting all the information inside implicit networks. These methods became prominent because they can train radiance fields in a remarkably short time. Besides representing existing 2D image data in 3D space, recent research has also explored ways of generating completely new 3D objects. With text-to-image embedding models like CLIP, various methods have been proposed to train implicit networks that generate new objects only from text prompts. This trend got faster with text-to-image diffusion generation models such as Stable Diffusion, especially through score distillation sampling (SDS), which conveys the representation of the text-to-image model to the NeRF model.

However, editing pre-trained 3D implicit networks according to specific conditions is still an open problem because of the constraints of the task: the integrity of the original 3D images has to be maintained while making the desired modifications. As initial work, several approaches tried to edit pre-trained NeRF models based on text conditions, using the pre-trained CLIP model to fine-tune the NeRF model parameters. But these methods have notable weaknesses, like the performance limitations of the CLIP model itself and the need to render high-resolution images during training, which takes a lot of time.

Recently several editing methods proposed to use the better expressiveness of text-to-image diffusion models such as Stable Diffusion. Some methods proposed to directly use the score distillation sampling method with additional regularizations. But these methods take a lot of time and are unstable in generation performance, because full-resolution rendering is required in the training stage and because of limitations of the score distillation loss itself. Other approaches proposed to directly manipulate the NeRF training images with text-guided image translation models. This method tries to make it possible to generate 3D images that correspond to text conditions. But it has a big drawback in training time, because the training images need to be translated periodically during the training process.

To address these challenges, we want to develop a new NeRF editing method that edits 3D scenes efficiently and effectively with only text prompts. For this, we let NeRF operate directly in the NeRF latent space, similar to Latent-NeRF, which helps reduce time and computational costs. But naively rendering the latent feature of real-world scenes directly with NeRF can lead to a big drop in view synthesis performance, since the latent space lacks geometric consistency. To deal with this issue, we analyze the latent generation process and propose a novel refinement layer based on the analysis to enhance performance. Also, to solve the drawback of the existing SDS-based method in editing, we propose a new sampling strategy that extends Delta Denoising Score (DDS), a 2D image editing technique based on score distillation sampling, into the 3D domain. With this extension we get high-performance editing capabilities while computational costs stay affordable, even with large Diffusion Models such as Stable Diffusion. Because our approach is so good at editing, we named it ED-NeRF (EDiting NeRF).

steps.text:
In recent years there has been remarkable progress in neural implicit representation for embedding three-dimensional images in neural networks. Because of this, it is now possible to render images from all angles with only a limited set of training viewpoints. Starting from the first well-known work, the Neural Radiance Field (NeRF) [1], which trained radiance fields with a simple MLP network, various improved techniques [2,3,4] have been proposed that are based on advanced network architectures or modified encoding. As an alternative, several methods [5,6,7,8] proposed to directly optimize voxel points that serve as sources for rendering, skipping the traditional approach of putting all the information inside implicit networks. These methods became prominent because they can train radiance fields in a remarkably short time. Besides representing existing 2D image data in 3D space, recent research has also explored ways of generating completely new 3D objects. With text-to-image embedding models like CLIP [9], various methods have been proposed to train implicit networks that generate new objects only from text prompts [10]. This trend got faster with text-to-image diffusion generation models such as Stable Diffusion [11], especially through score distillation sampling (SDS) [12], which conveys the representation of the text-to-image model to the NeRF model.

However, editing pre-trained 3D implicit networks according to specific conditions is still an open problem because of the constraints of the task: the integrity of the original 3D images has to be maintained while making the desired modifications. As initial work, several approaches [13,14] tried to edit pre-trained NeRF models based on text conditions, using the pre-trained CLIP model to fine-tune the NeRF model parameters. But these methods have notable weaknesses, like the performance limitations of the CLIP model itself and the need to render high-resolution images during training, which takes a lot of time.

Recently several editing methods proposed to use the better expressiveness of text-to-image diffusion models such as Stable Diffusion. Some methods [15] proposed to directly use the score distillation sampling method with additional regularizations. But these methods take a lot of time and are unstable in generation performance, because full-resolution rendering is required in the training stage and because of limitations of the score distillation loss itself. Other approaches [16] proposed to directly manipulate the NeRF training images with text-guided image translation models. This method tries to make it possible to generate 3D images that correspond to text conditions. But it has a big drawback in training time, because the training images need to be translated periodically during the training process.

To address these challenges, we want to develop a new NeRF editing method that edits 3D scenes efficiently and effectively with only text prompts. For this, we let NeRF operate directly in the NeRF latent space, similar to Latent-NeRF [17], which helps reduce time and computational costs. Because our approach is so good at editing, we named it ED-NeRF (EDiting NeRF).

steps.name: revised_draft
steps.text:
In recent years, neural implicit representation for embedding three-dimensional images in neural networks has seen remarkable progress, making it possible to render images from all angles using only a limited set of training viewpoints. Starting with the seminar work known as the Neural Radiance Field (NeRF) [1], which trained radiance fields using a simple MLP network, various improved techniques [2,3,4] based on advanced network architectures or modified encoding have been proposed. Alternatively, several methods [5,6,7,8] proposed to directly optimize voxel points serving as sources for rendering, bypassing the traditional approach of putting all information within implicit networks; these methods have gained prominence for training radiance fields in a remarkably short time. Beyond representing existing 2D image data in the 3D space, recent research has explored approaches for generating entirely novel 3D objects. With the emergence of text-to-image embedding models like CLIP [9], various methods have been proposed to train implicit networks that generate new objects solely from text prompts [10]. This trend has accelerated with the advent of text-to-image diffusion generation models such as Stable Diffusion [11], particularly through score distillation sampling (SDS) [12], which conveys the representation of the text-to-image model to the NeRF model.

However, editing pre-trained 3D implicit networks according to specific conditions still remains an open problem due to the constraints of the task: maintaining the integrity of the original 3D images while making the desired modifications. As initial work, several approaches [13,14] tried to edit pre-trained NeRF models based on text conditions, using the pre-trained CLIP model to fine-tune the parameters of NeRF models. Nevertheless, these methods exhibit notable weaknesses, including the performance limitations of the CLIP model itself and the need to render high-resolution images during training, which results in significant time consumption.

Recently, several editing methods proposed to leverage the enhanced expressiveness of text-to-image diffusion models such as Stable Diffusion. Some methods [15] proposed to directly employ score distillation sampling with additional regularizations. However, these methods suffer from significant time consumption and unstable generation performance, due to the requirement of full-resolution rendering in the training stage and the limitations of the score distillation loss itself. Other approaches [16] proposed to directly manipulate the training images of NeRF using text-guided image translation models, aiming to enable the generation of 3D images corresponding to text conditions. However, this suffers from a significant drawback in training time, as it requires periodic translation of the training images during training.

To address these challenges, we aim to develop a novel NeRF editing method to efficiently and effectively edit 3D scenes using only text prompts. To this end, we enable NeRF to operate directly in the NeRF latent space, similar to Latent-NeRF [17], which helps reduce time and computational costs. However, naively rendering the latent feature of real-world scenes directly with NeRF may cause a significant drop in view synthesis performance due to the lack of geometric consistency in the latent space. To tackle this issue, we analyze the latent generation process and propose a novel refinement layer based on this analysis to enhance performance. Furthermore, to overcome the drawback of the existing SDS-based method in editing, we propose a new sampling strategy that extends Delta Denoising Score (DDS) [18], a 2D image editing technique based on score distillation sampling, into the 3D domain. This extension lets us achieve high-performance editing while keeping computational costs affordable, even with large Diffusion Models such as Stable Diffusion. Given the editing proficiency of our approach, we name it ED-NeRF (EDiting NeRF).
